analysis.time: Published on 2026-08-02. No specific event date is reported in the evidence.
analysis.location_and_population: Global, with specific focus on infants, older adults, and vulnerable populations such as premature babies, children with underlying diseases, and leukemia patients.
analysis.event: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infections in children under five and poses a persistent threat to child health worldwide. Early-infancy infection with RSV significantly increases the risk of developing childhood asthma, especially in children with a family history of allergy or asthma. RSV also causes severe outcomes and heart complications in older adults.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: RSV leads to high hospitalization rates in adults, with a large real-world randomized trial in Denmark finding that the RSVpreF vaccine reduced RSV-related hospitalizations in adults aged 60 and over by over 80%. A single dose of the RSV vaccine offers 58% protection against hospitalization in older adults, but effectiveness varies in immunocompromised individuals. Year-round access to RSV immunization may reduce major seasonal outbreaks across the nation.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Pediatric experts are preparing for an expected rise in cases of RSV during the respiratory virus season. Maternal vaccination and nirsevimab together offer complementary strategies to protect newborns during their highest-risk months. The World Health Organization (WHO) has published its first-ever position paper on immunization products to protect infants against RSV. However, HEPA purifiers do not fully reduce classroom viral exposure, suggesting additional interventions are needed.

analysis.brief_en: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) remains a significant global health threat, particularly affecting infants and older adults. Early RSV infection in infancy increases the risk of childhood asthma, especially in children with a family history of allergy or asthma. For older adults, RSV causes severe outcomes and heart complications, with vaccines showing effectiveness in reducing hospitalizations by over 80% in adults aged 60 and over. Maternal vaccination and nirsevimab provide complementary protection for newborns during their highest-risk months. The WHO has issued its first position paper on RSV immunization for infants, emphasizing the need for year-round access to immunization to minimize seasonal outbreaks. Despite these advances, additional interventions are needed as HEPA purifiers alone do not fully reduce classroom viral exposure.
analysis.summary_en: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) remains a significant global health threat, particularly affecting infants and older adults. Early RSV infection in infancy increases the risk of childhood asthma, especially in children with a family history of allergy or asthma. For older adults, RSV causes severe outcomes and heart complications, with vaccines showing effectiveness in reducing hospitalizations by over 80% in adults aged 60 and over. Maternal vaccination and nirsevimab provide complementary protection for newborns during their highest-risk months. The WHO has issued its first position paper on RSV immunization for infants, emphasizing the need for year-round access to immunization to minimize seasonal outbreaks. Despite these advances, additional interventions are needed as HEPA purifiers alone do not fully reduce classroom viral exposure.

title: Enanta Pharmaceuticals to Present Data for Zelicapavir, an Oral, Once-Daily, N-Protein Inhibitor, in Development for the Treatment of Respiratory Syncytial Virus, at IDWeekTM 2026 - BioSpace

analysis.time: The event is scheduled for Thursday, October 22, 2026, from 12:15 PM to 1:30 PM ET. The conference itself runs from October 21-24, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The presentation will take place at the Walter E. Washington Convention Center in Washington, DC, as part of the IDWeekTM 2026 virtual and in-person event. The target population is high-risk adults.
analysis.event: Enanta Pharmaceuticals will present data on zelicapavir, an oral, once-daily N-protein inhibitor in development for the treatment of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), at IDWeekTM 2026. The data comes from a global, randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The trial involved high-risk adults, but no specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers are reported in the supplied evidence. The risk level is not explicitly stated.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The data will be presented at the conference platform during the event and on the company’s website. No further details on the investigation, testing, or response measures are provided in the evidence.

analysis.brief_en: Enanta Pharmaceuticals is set to present data on zelicapavir, an oral, once-daily N-protein inhibitor, at IDWeekTM 2026. The data is from a global, randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial targeting high-risk adults with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The presentation is scheduled for Thursday, October 22, 2026, at 12:15 PM to 1:30 PM ET in Poster Hall B-C at the Walter E. Washington Convention Center in Washington, DC. The conference runs from October 21-24, 2026, with virtual participation. The poster will also be available on the conference platform and the company’s website. No specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers are reported in the evidence, and the risk level is not explicitly stated. The event is a non-urgent update on drug development, not an outbreak or public health emergency.
